transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Honestly, what pushed me to come in is the tension. My shoulders and neck are clenched pretty much all day, like I’m bracing for a classroom observation that never ends. By the evening my jaw aches so much that I can barely enjoy playing guitar.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried about things even when there’s no obvious reason, like when you’re alone or trying to relax?

Yes. Even when nothing is happening, my mind just keeps going. I’ll be trying to sit quietly and it jumps from worrying whether I’ll ever get hired again, to thinking I’ve ruined my reputation with parents, to whether retirement is slipping away from me. And then I’ll get stuck on something small, like if I made a mistake during a story-time activity, and suddenly I’m wondering if that means I shouldn’t be trusted with children. It feels hard to shut off.
Do you find that you worry excessively about a number of different things, more days than not, and has this been going on for at least six months?

Yes, it’s definitely about a lot of different things, not just one. My mind keeps circling around whether I’ll ever get hired again, whether I’ve ruined my reputation with parents, whether retirement is slipping away… and then even small things, like a mistake during story-time, turn into me thinking maybe I shouldn’t be trusted with children. It feels excessive to me.
Do you find it really hard to control or stop the worrying, even when you try to focus on something else or tell yourself not to think about it?

Yes, very hard. I’ll tell myself, okay, just make a list, or pray for a minute, or go weed the garden and focus on the next practical thing. But it doesn’t really stop. One worry sort of hands off to the next one, and before I know it I’ve lost half the afternoon to it.
Do you ever feel physically restless, on edge, or unable to sit still when you’re anxious?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I feel wound up inside, but I haven’t paid much attention to whether I’m actually restless or unable to sit still. I don’t know that I’d describe it that way.
Do you ever feel fatigued or like you’re running on empty because of all the worrying?
I’m not really sure. I do get tired, but I don’t know if it’s because of the worrying or just the day itself. I haven’t paid close enough attention to say for sure.
Do you find that your worries interfere with your sleep, like trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or waking up feeling unrefreshed?

Yes. Most nights I get into bed and my mind just keeps going—replaying things I said in interviews, bills, licensing forms, all of it. I can be there for hours not really sleeping. And even when I do fall asleep, I’ll wake up around four already tense, thinking through what could go wrong that day.
Do you often feel muscle tension, such as tightness in your neck, shoulders, or jaw, especially when you're feeling anxious or stressed?

Yes. That’s actually one of the main reasons I came in. My shoulders and neck feel clenched almost all day, like I’m bracing for something that never ends. By the evening my jaw can ache so much that I don’t even enjoy playing guitar.
Do you find yourself getting irritable or easily annoyed, especially when you're feeling anxious or overwhelmed?
I’m not sure, honestly. I mean, I get annoyed like anyone does, but I haven’t really noticed a clear pattern where it’s because I’m anxious or overwhelmed. I’d have to think about that more.
Do you find it hard to concentrate or keep your mind on what you're doing because of worry or anxiety?

Yes, definitely. If I’m filling out applications or even trying to plan a simple lesson, I’ll read the same paragraph over and over. My mind keeps jumping to what an administrator might think of me, or whether I missed some important detail. It makes it really hard to stay on the task in front of me.
Would you say that your worrying and anxiety happen more often than not, like on most days, rather than just occasionally or in response to specific stressors?

Yes, it’s most days. It’s not just when something specific happens. My mind keeps circling around whether I’ll ever get hired again, whether I’ve ruined my reputation with parents, whether retirement is slipping away… and then it can get as small as thinking one mistake during story time means I shouldn’t be trusted with children anymore. It just keeps going.
Would you say that your anxiety and worry are present most days, even when nothing specific is happening, and do they often feel difficult to control or manage?

Yes. It’s there most days, and it’s hard to shut off. I’ll try to do something practical, like make a list, or pray, or go weed the garden, or just focus on the next step. But then one worry turns into the next one, and before I know it I’ve lost half the afternoon just going over things in my head.
